Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: VectorHealth POC: workload declaration & acceptance criteria

Thanks again for the productive call today — appreciate the clear background on your multi-tenant inference pattern. Summary + request below so we can finalize the POC intake and get the Dedicated trial scheduled.

High-level POC goals (as we discussed)
- Validate median latency <= 300ms for standard text-gen flows at your steady-state load
- Peak bursts handled without Fallback (graceful degradation only) up to 3x baseline for 3 minutes
- Cost / token baseline for 100k generated tokens/day with our recommended batching/kv cache

Immediate asks (items to attach / confirm)
1) Workload declaration (CSV): sample RPS ranges, typical token lengths for prompt & completion, concurrency, and expected burst cadence. Please use the attached template if helpful.
2) Acceptance criteria confirmation: which of the three goals above are deal breakers vs. stretch targets?
3) Technical contact + windows for scheduled soak tests (timezone PST).

Next steps / owners
- VectorHealth: provide workload CSV + confirm criteria by Tue 2027-06-01 (Sally)
- Redwood: produce POC evaluation plan and provisional infra sizing by Wed 2027-06-02 (Karthik)

From: Sally Park <sally.park@vectorhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@vectorhealth.com>, ops@vectorhealth.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VectorHealth POC: workload declaration & acceptance criteria

Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. Attached is our first pass: workload-declaration.csv (small sample extract from our staging fleet). A few clarifying notes inline: 

- Steady-state: 12 RPS average on the inference gateway, ~3 concurrent worker slots per request (we fan-out internal enrichment calls before generation)
- Prompt lengths: median prompt 85 tokens, 95th pct 240 tokens. Completion target avg 64 tokens.
- Burst pattern: typically 180–240s windows where RPS spikes to 40–45 (roughly 3–4x) driven by scheduled notifications; rare larger spikes during marketing sends but those are handled by an upstream queue we won't include in POC.
- KV cache: we have a 6-hour TTL used by product; expect >30% cache hit on repeated prompts within a session.

Acceptance criteria: we can commit to latency <= 350ms median for the flows that touch enrichment. The 300ms target is aggressive because of the enrichment fan-out; 350ms would be our baseline deal requirement. 99th pct under 1.2s is acceptable.

Owners: Sally (product) and Tom (infra) will own delivery of the CSV and support for soak windows.

[Attachment: workload-declaration.csv (CSV, 14KB)]

Hi all — tagging on with a concise eval plan that maps to the CSV Sally shared. Copying it into the thread for traceability.

POC evaluation checklist (pass/fail items)
- Median latency (enrichment flow) <= 350ms — pass/fail
- 95th percentile latency <= 800ms — pass/fail
- 99th percentile latency <= 1.2s (graceful degradation allowed) — informational
- Sustained throughput: maintain 12 RPS steady-state with <= 5% error rate for 30 minutes — pass/fail
- Burst handling: survive 3-minute burst at 40 RPS with no hard failures (errors < 1%) — pass/fail
- Cost baseline: projected per-1M-token cost with recommended batching <= vendor threshold (we'll compute after sizing) — informational/pass based on finance signoff

Test plan highlights
- Synthetic replay: use your provided CSV to synthesize request shapes and token lengths, inject enrichment fan-out latency (80–120ms) to match staging observed behavior.
- Cache modeling: enable 30% hit-rate in harness for results with and without cache to quantify savings.
- Rollout plan: start with a single-region Dedicated cluster (us-west1), run soak, then mirror to a second region if successful.

Deliverables and timeline
- Wed 2027-06-02: infra sizing + initial cost estimate (Karthik)
- Thu 2027-06-03: evaluation checklist posted to HubSpot and Drive (Marissa)
- Thu 2027-06-10: scheduled soak window (pending VectorHealth confirmation)
- Fri 2027-06-11: readout + next-step recommendations (team)

Ben and I will support the actual traffic injection and monitoring. Tom — once you confirm the network allowlist and service-account token exchange approach, we can provision the Dedicated trial.

Marissa Cole
